comments.text: Lines 7-10. `*FX200,2` writes 2 to the MOS's BREAK and ESCAPE byte (&0258), so BREAK clears memory rather than letting OLD bring the program back; `*FX220,144` makes character 144 (&90, the code SHIFT-f0 gives) the escape character, so the ESCAPE key no longer stops the program and SHIFT-f0 does; both hold through every program the menu chains. MODE 7, and ON ERROR RUN, which starts the menu again after any error, ESCAPE by SHIFT-f0 included.

Line 100, the title. A%=FALSE tells the program chained next that it starts afresh (the worksheet program K skips its printer question when A% is non-zero; the adventures keep their progress only while it is). @%=0 sets the print format. PROCB draws a cyan box over rows 3-8 with `4Mat Educational Software` in its top edge and `F L O W E R S  of  C R Y S T A L` across rows 5 and 6 in double height, blue letters on a cyan band (codes &8D, &86, &9D, &84); VDU 28 then makes rows 10-24 the text window, so that CLS in the menu leaves the title.

Lines 200-205, the menu. Each time round: CLS of the window, a cyan box (PROCB) holding the four choices in white, `1. Crystal - The Story`, `2. The Adventure (Part 1)`, `3. The Adventure (Part 2)` and `4. Utility (printer)`, `*FX15,0` to empty the keyboard buffer, then INPUT `Please choose (1-4)`, until the answer is exactly 1, 2, 3 or 4.
Line 210: CHAIN the program chosen: STORY (1), N1 (2, which leads to part 1), N2 (3, part 2) or K (4, the worksheets). Each loads at PAGE over this one.

PROCB(a,b,s,ln,c), lines 28900-28910: a box of teletext graphics from row a to row b, its left edge at column s and its inside ln wide, in graphics colour c (c+144). The corners are graphics characters h, 4, * and % (sixels for a rounded corner), the top and bottom rows a run of commas (a thin line), the sides 5 and j. Each middle row prints the left side, white text (&87), then TAB(ln): BASIC counts that from the 5 just printed (TAB(x,y) does not reset its count), so TAB(ln) prints ln-2 spaces, clearing the inside, and puts the right side under the corners.

PROCb(y1,y2,x,q$), line 29050: prints q$ at column x of every row from y1 to y2, most often a colour code and a new-background code that turn a band of rows into a coloured panel. Nothing in this program calls it; the adventures and the other programs carry the same procedure.
